The Leader microservice has as its main function the routing of all communications to the corresponding microservice within the system architecture.

The portal microservice has as its main function to offer a centralized interface for access to the different VWGS applications. [...] The portal microservice incorporates the binaries necessary for the frontEnd both of the portal itself and of the rest of the portal applications.

The client, which we also call frontEnd, is responsible for the presentation and user experience of the application, encapsulating the logic of the interface and the coordination of calls to the server's API.

The communication between the two components is done through an exchange of messages following standard network protocols and using interoperable data representation formats. [...] The protocol for exchanging messages used in this case is HTTP and the data format used is JSON.
The microservices are connected to a shared database decoupled by microservice and client.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The application has an architecture based on microservices, consisting of dividing the system into a set of small, independent, and autonomous services.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application is designed, deployed, and executed using cloud services instead of local or physical servers.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application follows the Client-Server pattern which organizes the code into two differentiated components: the client, which formulates service requests, and the server, which receives, processes, and returns responses.

patterns.name: MVVM
patterns.description: Angular applies the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) pattern, as its architecture is based on components and services.

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: Spring Boot organizes the code following the layered pattern with which responsibilities are separated.
